segments.arabic: [550] حدثنا عمرو بن عاصم قال: حدثنا همام عن قتادة عن أنس أن زيد بن ثابت حدثه
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Asim related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that Zayd ibn Thabit related to him:

segments.arabic: أنهم تسحروا مع النبي ﷺ ثم قاموا إلى الصلاة قلت: كم بينهما قال قدر خمسين أو ستين
segments.english: They ate the pre-dawn meal with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then stood up for prayer. I said: “How much time was between the two?” He said: “The amount of fifty or sixty,”

segments.arabic: يعني آيه
segments.english: meaning verses.

notes: The selected chain leaves the questioner unnamed, and the English does likewise. Both alternative counts remain; the closing explanation meaning verses is a distinct transmission remark. No conversion to minutes is added.

segments.arabic: [551] حدثنا حسن بن صباح سمع روحا حدثنا سعيد عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Hasan ibn Sabbah related to us. He heard Rawh: Sa‘id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ وزيد بن ثابت تسحرا فلما فرغا من سحورهما قام نبي الله ﷺ إلى الصلاة فصلى قلنا لأنس كم كان بين فراغهما من سحورهما ودخولهما في الصلاة قال قدر ما يقرأ الرجل خمسين آية
segments.english: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Zayd ibn Thabit ate the pre-dawn meal. When they had finished their pre-dawn meal, the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up for prayer and prayed. We said to Anas: “How long was it between their finishing their pre-dawn meal and their beginning the prayer?” He said: “The time in which a man recites fifty verses.”

notes: The selected Hasan ibn Sabbah is retained without the article found in the historical print. He heard Rawh and Sa‘id related to us remain distinct reporting formulas. We said to Anas is plural in the selected Arabic, unlike the Khan-family I.

segments.arabic: [552] حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبي أويس عن أخيه عن سليمان عن أبي حازم أنه سمع سهل بن سعد يقول:
segments.english: Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways related to us, from his brother, from Sulayman, from Abu Hazim, that he heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d say:

segments.arabic: كنت أتسحر في أهلي ثم يكون سرعة بي أن أدرك صلاة الفجر مع رسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: I used to eat the pre-dawn meal with my family, then hurry so that I could catch the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The brother and the short Sulayman remain as selected; no names are supplied from outside the paragraph. The account describes hurrying after the meal, without adding a fixed interval.

segments.arabic: [553] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: أخبرنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير أن عائشة أخبرته قالت
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth informed us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him. She said:

segments.arabic: كن نساء المؤمنات يشهدن مع رسول الله ﷺ صلاة الفجر متلفعات بمروطهن ثم ينقلبن إلى بيوتهن حين يقضين الصلاة لا يعرفهن أحد من الغلس
segments.english: The believing women used to attend the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wrapped in their garments. Then they would return to their homes when they had finished the prayer, and no one would recognise them because of the darkness at dawn.

notes: Darkness at dawn provisionally renders ghalas. The return is after the prayer; no claim that Fajr precedes dawn, garment specification or face-covering rule is inserted.

segments.arabic: [554] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار وعن بسر بن سعيد وعن الأعرج يحدثونه عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, and from Busr ibn Sa‘id, and from al-A‘raj—they related to him from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من أدرك من الصبح ركعة قبل أن تطلع الشمس فقد أدرك الصبح ومن أدرك ركعة من العصر قبل أن تغرب الشمس فقد أدرك العصر
segments.english: “Whoever catches a rak‘ah of the morning prayer before the sun rises has caught the morning prayer, and whoever catches a rak‘ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught ‘Asr.”

notes: All three parallel informants of Zayd and their plural reporting formula remain. Neither in its proper time nor a new legal explanation is added to the repeated has caught wording.

segments.arabic: [555] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من أدرك ركعة من الصلاة فقد أدرك الصلاة
segments.english: “Whoever catches a rak‘ah of the prayer has caught the prayer.”

notes: The short statement and full chain remain. The selected report does not explicitly say in time; that qualification from the Khan-family comparison is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [556] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا هشام عن قتادة عن أبي العالية عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-‘Aliyah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: شهد عندي رجال مرضيون وأرضاهم عندي عمر أن النبي ﷺ نهى عن الصلاة بعد الصبح حتى تشرق الشمس وبعد العصر حتى تغرب
segments.english: Men whom I trusted testified before me—and the one I trusted most among them was ‘Umar—that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until it sets.

notes: The complete Ibn Abbas frame and the distinction of Umar remain; the Khan-family body omits that frame. The selected tashruq is sunrise, distinct from the rising higher wording elsewhere.

segments.arabic: [557] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن شعبة عن قتادة سمعت أبا العالية عن ابن عباس قال: حدثني ناس بهذا
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Qatadah: I heard Abu al-‘Aliyah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Some people related to me about this.

segments.arabic: [558] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن هشام قال: أخبرني أبي قال: أخبرني ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me. He said: Ibn ‘Umar informed me. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: لا تحروا بصلاتكم طلوع الشمس ولا غروبها،
segments.english: “Do not seek out sunrise or sunset for your prayer.”

segments.arabic: وقال: حدثني ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: And he said: Ibn ‘Umar related to me. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا طلع حاجب الشمس فأخروا الصلاة حتى ترتفع وإذا غاب حاجب الشمس فأخروا الصلاة حتى تغيب
segments.english: “When the edge of the sun appears, delay the prayer until it rises higher; and when the edge of the sun disappears, delay the prayer until it disappears completely.”

segments.arabic: تابعه عبدة
segments.english: ‘Abdah corroborated him.

notes: The selected entry includes two sayings, the renewed Ibn Umar reporting formula and Abdah’s corroboration. The modern print numbers the sayings separately as 582 and 583; the selected complete entry stays together. The Khan-family comparison omits the final Abdah remark.

Edge of the sun preserves the selected hajib image. The distinctions between seeking out a time, the edge appearing or disappearing, and completing the sunset are retained without importing other accounts.

segments.arabic: [559] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل عن أبي أسامة عن عبيد الله عن خبيب بن عبد الرحمن عن حفص بن عاصم عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ نهى عن بيعتين وعن لبستين وعن صلاتين نهى عن الصلاة بعد الفجر حتى تطلع الشمس وبعد العصر حتى تغرب الشمس وعن اشتمال الصماء وعن الاحتباء في ثوب واحد يفضي بفرجه إلى السماء وعن المنابذة والملامسة
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two kinds of sale, two ways of dressing and two prayers. He forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until the sun sets; ishtimal al-samma’; sitting in ihtiba’ in a single garment with one’s private parts exposed towards the sky; and munabadhah and mulamasah.

notes: The four technical names are retained rather than replacing them with explanations absent from this paragraph. The complete bodily-exposure clause, the initial two sales/two dress forms/two prayers ordering and both prayer intervals remain. External definitions belong in separate reviewed context, not inside this quotation.

segments.arabic: [560] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: لا يتحرى أحدكم فيصلي عند طلوع الشمس ولا عند غروبها
segments.english: “None of you should seek out the time of sunrise or sunset to pray.”

notes: The separate repeated account and full chain remain. The wording concerns deliberately seeking those times; no additional qualification or ruling is supplied.

segments.arabic: [561] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن صالح عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني عطاء بن يزيد الجندعي أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري يقول: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Junda‘i informed me that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

segments.arabic: لا صلاة بعد الصبح حتى ترتفع الشمس ولا صلاة بعد العصر حتى تغيب الشمس
segments.english: “There is no prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises higher, and there is no prayer after ‘Asr until the sun sets.”

notes: The full selected al-Jundai attribution remains. Rises higher renders tartafi, distinct from the sunrise verb in 556; the wording is not flattened to match another report.

segments.arabic: [562] حدثنا محمد بن أبان قال: حدثنا غندر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي التياح قال: سمعت حمران بن أبان يحدث عن معاوية قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Aban related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard Humran ibn Aban relating from Mu‘awiyah, who said:

segments.arabic: إنكم لتصلون صلاة لقد صحبنا رسول الله ﷺ فما رأيناه يصليها ولقد نهى عنهما
segments.english: “You are indeed praying a prayer! We accompanied the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and never saw him pray it, and he forbade the two,”

segments.arabic: يعني الركعتين بعد العصر
segments.english: meaning the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.

notes: The selected plural we accompanied/we saw is retained, unlike the singular Khan-family body. The change from a prayer to the two remains, with the closing explanation as a separate transmission remark.

segments.arabic: [564] حدثنا أبو النعمان حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

segments.arabic: أصلي كما رأيت أصحابي يصلون لا أنهى أحدا يصلي بليل ولا نهار ما شاء غير أن لا تحروا طلوع الشمس ولا غروبها
segments.english: “I pray as I saw my companions pray. I do not forbid anyone to pray at night or by day as much as he wishes, except that you should not seek out sunrise or sunset.”

notes: This is Ibn Umar’s statement, not a newly attributed Prophetic saying. The selected change of address in the final exception remains. The four names introducing the chapter are preserved separately as Arabic chapter material.

segments.arabic: [565] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد بن أيمن قال: حدثني أبي أنه سمع عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman related to us. He said: My father related to me that he heard ‘A’ishah say:

segments.arabic: والذي ذهب به ما تركهما حتى لقي الله وما لقي الله تعالى حتى ثقل عن الصلاة وكان يصلي كثيرا من صلاته قاعدا
segments.english: “By the One who took him away, he never left them until he met Allah. He did not meet Allah, exalted is He, until prayer had become burdensome for him, and he used to perform many of his prayers sitting,”

segments.arabic: تعني الركعتين بعد العصر
segments.english: she means the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.

segments.arabic: وكان النبي ﷺ يصليهما ولا يصليهما في المسجد مخافة أن يثقل على أمته وكان يحب ما يخفف عنهم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray them, but he did not pray them in the mosque for fear of burdening his community, and he loved what made things easier for them.

notes: The opening oath, pronouns and divine honorific remain. Many is not changed to most; standing is not supplied where the selected paragraph says prayer. The explanatory she means is kept distinct from the account.

segments.arabic: [566] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى قال: حدثنا هشام قال: أخبرني أبي قالت عائشة
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father informed me: ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: بن أختي ما ترك النبي ﷺ السجدتين بعد العصر عندي قط
segments.english: “Son of my sister, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never left the two prostrations after ‘Asr with me.”

notes: The nephew address remains. The selected sajdatayn is rendered two prostrations, consistent with sajdah in 531, rather than silently rewriting the Arabic to rakatayn. The two English comparisons use rakahs in this prayer context; this lexical distinction remains provisional.

segments.arabic: [567] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد قال: حدثنا الشيباني قال: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن الأسود عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-Shaybani related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: ركعتان لم يكن رسول الله ﷺ يدعهما سرا ولا علانية ركعتان قبل صلاة الصبح وركعتان بعد العصر
segments.english: “Two rak‘ahs that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not leave, in private or in public: two rak‘ahs before the morning prayer and two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.”

notes: The selected opening dual and both subsequent pairs remain. The English does not silently replace the opening two with four, or add locations not named in the paragraph.

segments.arabic: [568] حدثنا محمد بن عرعرة قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي إسحاق قال: رأيت الأسود ومسروقا شهدا على عائشة قالت
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I saw al-Aswad and Masruq testify concerning ‘A’ishah that she said:

segments.arabic: ما كان النبي ﷺ يأتيني في يوم بعد العصر إلا صلى ركعتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never came to me on a day after ‘Asr without praying two rak‘ahs.

notes: Both named witnesses, Abu Ishaq’s I saw and the testimony formula remain; they are not reduced to a direct Aishah attribution.

segments.arabic: [569] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى هو ابن أبي كثير عن أبي قلابة أن أبا المليح حدثه قال
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya—he is Ibn Abi Kathir—from Abu Qilabah, that Abu al-Malih related to him. He said:

segments.arabic: كنا مع بريدة في يوم ذي غيم، فقال بكروا بالصلاة فإن النبي ﷺ قال: من ترك صلاة العصر حبط عمله
segments.english: We were with Buraydah on a cloudy day, and he said: “Pray early, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his work has come to nothing.’”

notes: The selected Abu al-Malih, plural we and Yahya name clarification remain. The Khan-family heading says Ibn Abu al-Malih and its body uses I; those forms are not imported. No expedition context is added from another account. Work follows the rendering in 528 without adding all good deeds.

segments.arabic: [570] حدثنا عمران بن ميسرة قال: حدثنا محمد بن فضيل قال: حدثنا حصين عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال
segments.english: ‘Imran ibn Maysarah related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: سرنا مع النبي ﷺ ليلة، فقال بعض القوم لو عرست بنا يا رسول الله قال أخاف أن تناموا عن الصلاة قال بلال أنا أوقظكم فاضطجعوا وأسند بلال ظهره إلى راحلته فغلبته عيناه فنام فاستيقظ النبي ﷺ وقد طلع حاجب الشمس، فقال: يا بلال أين ما قلت: قال: ما ألقيت علي نومة مثلها قط قال إن الله قبض أرواحكم حين شاء وردها عليكم حين شاء يا بلال قم فأذن بالناس بالصلاة فتوضأ فلما ارتفعت الشمس وابيضت قام فصلى
segments.english: We travelled with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night. Some of the people said: “If only you would stop for us to rest, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “I fear that you will sleep through the prayer.” Bilal said: “I will wake you.” They lay down, and Bilal rested his back against his mount. His eyes overcame him and he slept. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, awoke when the edge of the sun had appeared. He said: “Bilal, where is what you said?” He said: “Never has sleep like this come upon me.” He said: “Allah took your souls when He wished and returned them to you when He wished. Bilal, get up and call the people to prayer.” He performed ablution, and when the sun had risen higher and become bright, he stood up and prayed.

notes: The full sequence of resting, Bilal’s promise, both awakenings, the question, reply and instruction remains. Rahilah is a mount, not the comparison’s saddle. The sun’s edge appearing and its later rising and brightening are separate stages; no fixed minutes are supplied. The Arabic past-tense took/returned is retained.

segments.arabic: [571] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة عن جابر بن عبد الله
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

segments.arabic: أن عمر بن الخطاب جاء يوم الخندق بعد ما غربت الشمس فجعل يسب كفار قريش قال: يا رسول الله ما كدت أصلي العصر حتى كادت الشمس تغرب قال النبي ﷺ والله ما صليتها فقمنا إلى بطحان فتوضأ للصلاة وتوضأنا لها فصلى العصر بعد ما غربت الشمس ثم صلى بعدها المغرب
segments.english: That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came on the day of the Ditch after the sun had set and began cursing the unbelievers of Quraysh. He said: “Messenger of Allah, I barely managed to pray ‘Asr before the sun was about to set.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” We got up and went to Buthan. He performed ablution for the prayer, and we performed ablution for it. He prayed ‘Asr after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

notes: The selected barely/about-to-set wording is retained, distinct from the shorter until it set in 573. Both ablutions, the oath, place and prayer order remain. The Khan-family rendering of Umar’s statement is not used to erase that distinction.

segments.arabic: [572] حدثنا أبو نعيم وموسى بن إسماعيل قالا: حدثنا همام عن قتادة عن أنس عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym and Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. They said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: من نسي صلاة فليصل إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك
segments.english: “Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray when he remembers it. There is no expiation for it except that.”

segments.arabic: وأقم الصلاة لذكري
segments.english: “And establish the prayer for My remembrance.”

segments.arabic: قال موسى قال همام سمعته يقول بعد { وأقم الصلاة للذكرى }،
segments.english: Musa said: Hammam said: I heard him later saying: “And establish the prayer for remembrance.”

segments.arabic: وقال حبان حدثنا همام حدثنا قتادة حدثنا أنس عن النبي ﷺ نحوه
segments.english: And Habban said: Hammam related to us. Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.

notes: The digital paragraph reverses the two quoted wordings. Both inspected prints give li-dhikri first and lil-dhikra in the later Musa/Hammam remark. Two separately evidenced corrections restore those words only, retaining the original digital paragraph and all surrounding transmission formulas.

The quoted command is a separate transmission segment: Ibn Hajar discusses disagreement over whether its citation is Qatadah’s or the Prophet’s. No Then he recited connector is inserted. The Musa/Hammam remark and complete closing Habban chain remain; both English comparisons abbreviate this material. Habban is vocalised with initial a in the commentary; the Arabic name itself is unchanged.

segments.arabic: [573] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن هشام قال: حدثنا يحيى هو ابن أبي كثير عن أبي سلمة عن جابر قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: Yahya—he is Ibn Abi Kathir—related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir, who said:

segments.arabic: جعل عمر يوم الخندق يسب كفارهم، وقال: ما كدت أصلي العصر حتى غربت قال: فنزلنا بطحان فصلى بعد ما غربت الشمس ثم صلى المغرب
segments.english: ‘Umar began cursing their unbelievers on the day of the Ditch, and said: “I could hardly pray ‘Asr until it set.” He said: “We went down to Buthan, and he prayed after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib.”

notes: The selected statement says until it set, without 571’s second almost. The first prayer in the closing sequence is unnamed in this shorter paragraph and remains unnamed in English. No longer account is substituted.

segments.arabic: [574] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى قال: حدثنا عوف قال: حدثنا أبو المنهال قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Awf related to us. He said: Abu al-Minhal related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: انطلقت مع أبي إلى أبي برزة الأسلمي، فقال له أبي حدثنا كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي المكتوبة قال: كان يصلي الهجير وهي التي تدعونها الأولى حين تدحض الشمس ويصلي العصر ثم يرجع أحدنا إلى أهله في أقصى المدينة والشمس حية ونسيت ما قال في المغرب قال: وكان يستحب أن يؤخر العشاء قال: وكان يكره النوم قبلها والحديث بعدها وكان ينفتل من صلاة الغداة حين يعرف أحدنا جليسه ويقرأ من الستين إلى المائة
segments.english: I went with my father to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. My father said to him: “Tell us how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the prescribed prayer.” He said: “He used to pray the midday prayer—which you call the first—when the sun declined, and he prayed ‘Asr, then one of us would return to his family in the furthest part of Madinah while the sun was bright. I have forgotten what he said about Maghrib.” He said: “He liked to delay ‘Isha’.” He said: “He disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He used to finish the morning prayer when one of us could recognise the person sitting beside him, and he would recite from sixty to a hundred.”

segments.arabic: [575] حدثنا عبد الله بن الصباح قال: حدثنا أبو علي الحنفي حدثنا قرة بن خالد قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sabbah related to us. He said: Abu ‘Ali al-Hanafi related to us. Qurrah ibn Khalid related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: انتظرنا الحسن وراث علينا حتى قربنا من وقت قيامه فجاء، فقال دعانا جيراننا هؤلاء،
segments.english: We waited for al-Hasan, and he was late in coming to us until we were close to his time for rising. He came and said: “These neighbours of ours invited us.”

segments.arabic: ثم قال: قال أنس
segments.english: Then he said: Anas said:

segments.arabic: نظرنا النبي ﷺ ذات ليلة حتى كان شطر الليل يبلغه فجاء فصلى لنا ثم خطبنا، فقال ألا إن الناس قد صلوا ثم رقدوا وإنكم لم تزالوا في صلاة ما انتظرتم الصلاة
segments.english: We waited for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night until it was approaching half the night. He came and led us in prayer, then addressed us, saying: “Indeed, the people have prayed and then gone to sleep, while you have continued in prayer as long as you have waited for the prayer.”

segments.arabic: قال الحسن وإن القوم لا يزالون بخير ما انتظروا الخير
segments.english: Al-Hasan said: “People continue to be in good as long as they wait for good.”

segments.arabic: قال قرة هو من حديث أنس عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Qurrah said: “It is from Anas’s hadith from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: The opening wait, al-Hasan’s delay and neighbours’ invitation, Anas’s account and both closing attributions remain. Ibn Hajar explains the rising time as the usual end of al-Hasan’s gathering and yablughuhu as approaching; neither a start-of-teaching gloss nor a new narrator chain for that verb is introduced.
The closing Qurrah attribution is kept as an explicit transmission remark rather than silently merging al-Hasan’s preceding sentence into the Prophetic quotation.

segments.arabic: [576] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: حدثني سالم بن عبد الله بن عمر وأبو بكر ابن أبي حثمة أن عبد الله بن عمر قال
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Hathmah related to me that ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ صلاة العشاء في آخر حياته فلما سلم قام النبي ﷺ، فقال أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه فإن رأس مائة لا يبقى ممن هو اليوم على ظهر الأرض أحد فوهل الناس في مقالة رسول الله ﷺ إلى ما يتحدثون من هذه الأحاديث عن مائة سنة وإنما قال النبي ﷺ لا يبقى ممن هو اليوم على ظهر الأرض يريد بذلك أنها تخرم ذلك القرن
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’ near the end of his life. When he had given the greeting of peace, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred, no one who is on the face of the earth today will remain.” The people misunderstood the statement of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taking it to mean what they say in these accounts about a hundred years. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, only said: “No one who is on the face of the earth today will remain,” intending by that the passing away of that generation.

notes: The selected Abu Bakr ibn Abi Hathmah is retained without supplying Sulayman from the comparison. The first hundred has no explicit unit in the selected paragraph or modern print, unlike the historical print; years is therefore not inserted there. The second occurrence explicitly says a hundred years.
The misunderstanding and generation explanation remain within Ibn Umar’s account, outside the Prophetic quotation. No additional end-of-world or lifespan explanation is inserted.

segments.arabic: [577] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا معتمر بن سليمان قال: حدثنا أبي حدثنا أبو عثمان عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: My father related to us. Abu ‘Uthman related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr:

segments.arabic: أن أصحاب الصفة كانوا أناسا فقراء وأن النبي ﷺ قال: من كان عنده طعام اثنين فليذهب بثالث وإن أربع فخامس أو سادس وأن أبا بكر جاء بثلاثة فانطلق النبي ﷺ بعشرة قال: فهو أنا وأبي وأمي
segments.english: That the people of the Suffah were poor people, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has food for two should take a third, and if for four, then a fifth or a sixth.” Abu Bakr brought three, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went off with ten. He said: “It was I, my father and my mother,”

segments.arabic: فلا أدري قال وامرأتي وخادم بيننا وبين بيت أبي بكر
segments.english: I do not know whether he said: “And my wife and a servant shared between us and Abu Bakr’s household.”

segments.arabic: وإن أبا بكر تعشى عند النبي ﷺ ثم لبث حيث صليت العشاء ثم رجع فلبث حتى تعشى النبي ﷺ فجاء بعد ما مضى من الليل ما شاء الله قالت له امرأته وما حبسك عن أضيافك أو قالت ضيفك قال أو ما عشيتيهم قالت أبوا حتى تجيء قد عرضوا فأبوا قال: فذهبت أنا فاختبأت، فقال: يا غنثر فجدع وسب، وقال كلوا لا هنيا، فقال والله لا أطعمه أبدا وأيم الله ما كنا نأخذ من لقمة إلا ربا من أسفلها أكثر منها
segments.english: Abu Bakr ate supper with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then remained where ‘Isha’ was prayed. Then he returned and stayed until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate supper. He came after as much of the night had passed as Allah wished. His wife said to him: “What kept you from your guests?”—or she said: “Your guest.” He said: “Did you not give them supper?” She said: “They refused until you came. It was offered to them, but they refused.” He said: “I went and hid.” He said: “Ghunthar!” Then he invoked mutilation against me and insulted me, and said: “Eat, without enjoyment!” He said: “By Allah, I will never eat it.” By Allah, whenever we took a morsel, more than it grew from beneath it.

segments.arabic: قال يعني حتى شبعوا وصارت أكثر مما كانت قبل ذلك
segments.english: He said, meaning: until they were full and it had become more than it was before.

segments.arabic: فنظر إليها أبو بكر فإذا هي كما هي أو أكثر منها، فقال لامرأته يا أخت بني فراس ما هذا قالت لا وقرة عيني لهي الآن أكثر منها قبل ذلك بثلاث مرات فأكل منها أبو بكر، وقال إنما كان ذلك من الشيطان
segments.english: Abu Bakr looked at it, and it was as it had been, or more. He said to his wife: “Sister of Banu Firas, what is this?” She said: “No, by the joy of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before.” Abu Bakr ate some of it and said: “That was only from Satan,”

segments.arabic: يعني يمينه
segments.english: meaning his oath.

segments.arabic: ثم أكل منها لقمة ثم حملها إلى النبي ﷺ فأصبحت عنده وكان بيننا وبين قوم عقد فمضى الأجل ففرقنا اثنى عشر رجلا مع كل رجل منهم أناس الله أعلم كم مع كل رجل فأكلوا منها أجمعون
segments.english: Then he ate a morsel of it and carried it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and it remained with him until morning. There was an agreement between us and some people, and its term expired. He divided us among twelve men, with people accompanying each of them—Allah knows how many were with each man—and they all ate from it,

segments.arabic: أو كما قال
segments.english: or as he said.

notes: The food counts, wife/servant uncertainty, guest/guests alternative, oaths, repeated eating and waiting, narrator explanations, treaty, twelve men and final uncertainty all remain. The uncertainty includes the wife and servant here, following both English comparisons and the related commentary; modern punctuation can restrict it to the wife. Its scope remains provisional.

Both inspected prints and the selected digital text read haythu, where, in the Isha clause. The English comparisons use until, a documented alternative Arabic reading; that alternative is not silently substituted. The repeated supper/return sequence stays in its selected order without importing the nap variant.

Ghunthar is retained as a harsh address rather than selecting one disputed English insult. Ibn Hajar explains jadda as a curse invoking mutilation, not a physical act; the following insult and uncomfortable eat without enjoyment wording are retained. The joy-of-my-eye phrase is kept as an oath rather than an address to Abu Bakr. Divided us among twelve men follows the commentary’s grouping reading, without adding military leaders or naming an unstated subject.
